page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.8xlarge is a dedicated high clock speed virtual server instance powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. The configuration provides 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates vector and cryptographic instruction sets, including AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, BMI2, and FMA.

The instance is provisioned with 128.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It features a baseline network throughput of 10 Gbps and operates without bundled local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating reliance on remote network-attached block storage for persistent data needs.

Benchmark testing demonstrates consistent mid-range execution across both general-purpose and compute-intensive workloads. The instance registers a PassMark CPU score of 29,517.51 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 11,107.0, supported by clang compilation test scores of 23,704.0. Memory sub-benchmarks yield 109.89 GB/sec read and 48.22 GB/sec write throughput on large blocks, driving in-memory performance such as 28.91 million Redis SET operations per second and 21.45 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. CPU-bound small-scale inference achieves 85.62 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model and 12.4 tokens per second on a 7B model.

With its combination of elevated 3.1 GHz clock rates and balanced memory allocation, the ecs.hfg6.8xlarge represents a balanced compute configuration. The absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated accelerators means cost efficiency depends heavily on network block storage utilization. It is particularly suited for high-throughput web serving, clustered application servers, software build pipelines, continuous integration systems, and in-memory caching nodes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.8xlarge is a high clock speed virtual instance based on KVM and the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores, supported by 35 MB of L3 cache, AVX-512 VNNI, and 128.0 GB of system memory (4.0 GB per vCPU). The instance contains no bundled local storage and zero GPU accelerators, offering a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations place it in the mid-tier performance band across common synthetic suites, recording a PassMark CPU score of 29,517.51, Geekbench multi-core score of 11,107.0, and 28.91 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. The system is structurally aligned with compute-focused enterprise workloads, compilation clusters, CI/CD orchestration, in-memory caching, and backend API routing requiring consistent single-core clock frequencies.
